findings.title: Workflow-start idempotency replay crosses platform-tenant boundaries
findings.resolution: Scope start-key lookup, replay, and uniqueness by platform tenant; validate tenant binding before replay.
findings.original_trigger: Two separately authenticated platform tenants start the same app/workflow with the same idempotency key and input.
findings.original_observation: Tenant B receives Tenant A's run ID and tenant identity; the response also exposes stored run data.

findings.title: A parked independent branch blocks for_each siblings and spins dispatch
findings.resolution: Restore running custody for ready foreach items and report progress only when an item actually advances.
findings.original_trigger: A timer root and independent two-item for_each root, with max_parallel=2.
findings.original_observation: Zero items execute; dispatch loops until cancellation in both MemStore and PgStore.

findings.title: Non-JSON successful HTTP responses bypass the retry budget
findings.resolution: Persist successful text responses as JSON strings and preserve recovered attempt numbers so retry budgets remain bounded.
findings.original_trigger: A normal declarative handler returns HTTP 200 with plain-text OK and retry.max_attempts=1.
findings.original_observation: Four consecutive ticks execute the handler four times; run stays pending and step attempt resets to zero.

findings.title: NUL characters in code-step errors cause unrecorded failures and requeue
findings.resolution: Clean PostgreSQL-bound error text and truncate safely on UTF-8 boundaries.
findings.original_trigger: A code step reports error text containing a NUL character, even with non_retryable=true.
findings.original_observation: PgStore rejects the write with SQLSTATE 22021; the run returns to pending without recording the step failure.

findings.title: Terminal replay responses may omit recorded operations without nondeterminism detection
findings.resolution: Report replay cursors in all SDKs; reject terminal responses that omit visited history or pending operations.
findings.original_trigger: A replay returns early after removing a previously recorded pending approval wait.
findings.original_observation: The Python SDK emits succeeded with no operations, and engine protocol validation accepts it.

findings.title: Python code-workflow SDK reports non-finite float results as successful invalid JSON
findings.resolution: Reject non-finite JSON values in the Python SDK and report a nonretryable step failure.
findings.original_trigger: A Python step returns float('nan') or infinity.
findings.original_observation: The SDK reports succeeded with an unrepresentable JSON float; JSON serialization emits NaN, which the Go entry protocol rejects.

findings.title: Timeout exception-route cycles pass DAG validation and strand runs
findings.resolution: Include timeout and failure routing edges in DAG cycle detection.
findings.original_trigger: A wait routes on_timeout to itself, or depends on its own timeout handler.
findings.original_observation: ValidateWorkflowDAG accepts both definitions; dispatch leaves every step pending, run running, and no wait timer registered.

findings.title: External event payload can impersonate the timeout sentinel
findings.resolution: Reject the reserved timeout-marker payload consistently at event and callback storage boundaries.
findings.original_trigger: An event wait with on_timeout receives the accepted payload {"timeout":true} before its deadline.
findings.original_observation: The timeout-only /notify handler executes and the run succeeds, in both MemStore and PgStore. The simulator rejects this payload shape but runtime ingestion accepts it.

findings.title: Internal HTML escaping kills code workflows with valid sub-limit input
findings.resolution: Disable HTML escaping for internal code-workflow request encoding while preserving transport bounds.
findings.original_trigger: A code workflow starts with a 614402-byte JSON string containing 600 KiB of less-than characters; input limit is 1048576 bytes.
findings.original_observation: The internal request grows to 3686544 bytes against a 2883584-byte limit; the run becomes dead before its handler is called. An equal-sized x-only string succeeds. Reproduced on both stores.

findings.title: Expired ordinary HTTP worker can overwrite a recovered terminal step result
findings.resolution: Preserve attempt numbers during recovery; reject stale starts, expired leases, and completions/retries for superseded attempts.
findings.original_trigger: A worker pauses beyond its lease; another worker reclaims the normal HTTP step and completes the run; the expired worker then records its old success.
findings.original_observation: Lease recovery reuses attempt 1 and resume generation 0. PgStore accepts the expired completion even after the replacement completed. The step output becomes {"worker":"expired"} while the succeeded run retains {"worker":"current"}.

findings.title: Python idle detection cancels valid nested asyncio.gather before the first durable operation
findings.resolution: Detect durable suspension from the actual awaited task graph rather than a fixed number of event-loop turns.
findings.original_trigger: A workflow reaches its first wf.step through eight nested asyncio.gather calls, without external I/O.
findings.original_observation: Depth 1 reaches the step. Depth 8 executes zero step bodies and returns ops=[] with result.status=running. The actual engine validator rejects this response because no operation is pending.

findings.title: Oversized errors bypass SDK response fitting, including NonRetryableError
findings.resolution: Bound step and terminal errors and reserve metadata for every parallel operation before allocating response bytes.
findings.original_trigger: A step raises a nonretryable error with a 2 MiB message.
findings.original_observation: Python emits 2097334 bytes and Go emits 2097317 bytes, both exceeding the 983040-byte SDK response cap. Both mark the operation non_retryable=true while leaving its error unbounded.

findings.title: Repeating a valid maximum-length operation name generates an invalid name after executing its body
findings.resolution: Accept canonical repeat suffixes beyond a valid 128-byte base; classify an exhausted operation budget as a terminal limit failure.
findings.original_trigger: A workflow calls a step twice with an accepted 128-character base name.
findings.original_observation: Python and Go append #2, generating a 130-character second operation name. Both step bodies have already executed. The actual engine validator rejects the Python SDK response as an invalid operation name.

findings.title: Gateway HTML escaping makes valid code-workflow output exceed the scheduler response limit
findings.resolution: Disable HTML escaping for authenticated native workflow gateway responses, retaining the scheduler response cap.
findings.original_trigger: A Python code step successfully returns a 200 KiB string of less-than characters. Its SDK response is 204963 bytes, below the 983040-byte response cap.
findings.original_observation: The production gateway handler returns HTTP 200 but HTML-escapes the JSON result to 1228998 bytes. The actual bounded decoder used by the scheduler rejects it at 1048576 bytes. An equal-sized x-only control becomes 204998 bytes and decodes successfully.

verification.scope: Focused workflow test selection used temporary Go test overlays to exclude unrelated test files; all production files were included. Native regression tests are in the repository.
verification.limitation: The earlier broad store sweep exceeded its 10-minute budget during fixture cloning. Focused store regressions and workflow conformance passed afterward; a full repository test run was not performed.

rollout: Apply expand migration 20261111160000000 before updating the control plane.
Upgrade all API replicas before applying contract migration 20261111160000001 in a full release.
Deploy the scheduler and internal gateway fixes, then redeploy applications with the updated workflow SDKs.
Full replay-cursor checks require the updated SDKs; older SDKs remain readable but may not omit pending operations.
The contract downgrade refuses shared cross-tenant keys until those keys are reconciled.
historical_evidence_note: Original audit evidence is retained in the saved session findings register. Native tests supersede the historical ingress-success expectation for GW-008 and the generated-name length expectation for GW-013.
